news.headline: NeurAxis Reports Record Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Driven by 116% Year-Over-Year Revenue Growth
news.summary: Q2 revenue rose 116% year-over-year to $1.93M with gross margin expanding 230 basis points to 85.9%, as the Category I CPT code for PENFS effective January 1, 2026 pushed more devices to full reimbursement price. Cash stood at $8.3M on June 30 after raising $2.5M in the quarter via the ATM facility and warrant redemptions, with lower operating cash outflows.

news.headline: Earnings Call Transcript: NeurAxis Falls on Q2 2026 EPS Miss Despite 116% Revenue Growth
news.summary: Shares fell after Q2 EPS of -$0.19 missed the -$0.16 consensus even though revenue beat on growth. Management named its three priorities as expanding insurance coverage, improving execution in already-covered markets and building the Veterans Affairs channel, and warned H2 operating expenses will rise as it hires sales, marketing, clinical and policy staff.

news.headline: NeurAxis (NRXS) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.summary: Full transcript in which management confirmed more than 100 million covered lives today and a target above 200 million by the end of 2027, plus a plan to have 10 commission-only (1099) Veterans Affairs territory representatives in the field by September 15, 2026. Executives said the rising opex is intended to pull the company toward cash-flow breakeven rather than delay it.

news.headline: NeurAxis (NRXS): Q2 2026 Earnings Review
news.summary: Independent review highlighted average selling price up 28% year-over-year to $992, closing in on the $1,195 list-price ceiling, and prior-authorization approval rates rising to 31% year-to-date from 12% a year earlier. It flagged the mid-September VA sales-force buildout as the main Q4 volume catalyst and noted management is cautiously optimistic on a major new payer coverage win in H2 2026 or early 2027.

news.headline: NeurAxis Expands Payer Coverage with New Policies
news.summary: New medical policies for PENFS added more than 500,000 covered lives, expanding access to IB-Stim for beneficiaries in the Mid-Atlantic region. The announcement continued the post-CPT-code march toward the company's stated goal of nationwide written policy coverage.

news.headline: NeurAxis Declares Q2 2026 Stock Dividend on Series B Preferred Stock
news.summary: The board declared the Q2 2026 stock dividend on the Series B Preferred, issuing roughly 80,463 common shares at a $2.38 calculation rate, payable July 29 to holders of record July 21. Routine non-cash preferred housekeeping that adds modest ongoing dilution rather than operational news.

catalysts.label: VA sales force fully staffed
catalysts.detail: Management committed on the Q2 call to having 10 commission-only (1099) Veterans Affairs territory representatives in the field by September 15, 2026, aimed at turning the VA channel into a Q4 IB-Stim volume driver.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.detail: Next quarterly report, expected around mid-November on the company's usual cadence (Q1 on May 12, Q2 on Aug 11). Key tests: whether triple-digit revenue growth holds, whether ASP keeps climbing toward the $1,195 list price, and how much the promised H2 opex step-up eats into the improving $1.0M quarterly cash burn.

catalysts.label: Major national payer coverage decision
catalysts.detail: Talks with two large commercial payers are progressing and management said it is cautiously optimistic about a coverage win in H2 2026 or early 2027; the CEO has described a single major payer add as a potential slingshot toward profitability.

catalysts.label: Covered lives above 200 million
catalysts.detail: Management reiterated on the Q2 call that it expects to exceed 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, roughly doubling from the 100 million-plus reached today, which requires a steady drumbeat of payer-policy wins like the August Mid-Atlantic addition.

pulse: NeurAxis's August 11 Q2 print confirmed the CPT-code reimbursement thesis is working - revenue up 116% year-over-year to $1.93M, gross margin 85.9%, ASP up 28% to $992, and cash burn down to about $1.0M a quarter on $8.3M of cash - but the stock sold off because EPS of -$0.19 missed the -$0.16 consensus and management guided to higher H2 operating expenses as it hires into sales, marketing, clinical and policy roles. The August 4 payer expansion (+500K Mid-Atlantic lives) kept the coverage drumbeat going, and no material company-specific news has come out since the print through August 19, so the tape is currently trading on positioning rather than fresh information. The story now hinges on execution: the 10-rep VA sales force due by September 15, the two large commercial payers in negotiation, and whether growth can outrun continued ATM/preferred dilution and the still-standing going-concern qualification.
